mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressures that may lead to tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased corporate costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above 0.5% MoM signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances when RSAFS MoM > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals a weakening supply side, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when INDPRO MoM < -1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1%, it signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2pp in the same month, it signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS > 200k & UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% MoM and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 0.5% MoM, it signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances when HOUST MoM > 5% & RSAFS MoM > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM coupled with an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals tightening supply and monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when INDPRO MoM < -1% & FEDFUNDS increase during late-cycle expansion.
